_comment: Authoring anchors for NEW CED Unit 3 (Inference for Proportions & Categorical Data; OLD topics 5.4-5.6, 6.x, and 8.1/8.4-8.6). Describe what a DOK-2 and a DOK-3 look like here so authors rate by the same yardstick (spec §1.1-1.2). Anchors DESCRIBE released-FRQ patterns; they never quote an item.

dok2_anchors.shape: Given a population proportion, sample size, and sampling method, check the 10 percent and Large Counts conditions, then compute the center, standard deviation, z-score, or tail probability for a sample proportion.
dok2_anchors.why_dok2: The model and target quantity are supplied, so the student follows a standard condition-check and calculation sequence with one statistical path.

dok2_anchors.shape: Given the hypotheses or confidence level and a named one-proportion, two-proportion, or chi-square procedure, calculate the statistic, standard error, interval, p-value, or expected counts and state the result in context.
dok2_anchors.why_dok2: Procedure selection and claim boundaries are already settled; the student executes a known multistep algorithm and communicates its numerical output.

dok3_anchors.shape: Two estimators or probability models compete; decide which is appropriate for the stated purpose by coordinating bias, variability, sampling method, and distribution conditions, then explain what the rejected criterion or approximation would mislead a reader into concluding.
dok3_anchors.why_dok3: The student must weigh multiple relevant properties against a specific goal and trace the practical consequence of a tempting but incomplete rule; no single calculation determines the judgment.

dok3_anchors.shape: Several categorical-data procedures are plausible; select one- versus two-proportion inference or chi-square goodness-of-fit, homogeneity, or independence from the variables, samples, and question, and explain what an alternative procedure would test instead.
dok3_anchors.why_dok3: The student translates a research question and study structure into a defensible procedure while ruling out alternatives that answer different questions.

dok3_anchors.shape: Two students interpret the same interval or test differently; decide which conclusion the evidence and conditions support, distinguish statistical significance from certainty or importance, and bound the conclusion to the population and design.
dok3_anchors.why_dok3: The student coordinates a numerical result, procedure conditions, error risk, and scope of inference to adjudicate competing claims and explain the consequence of the overreach.

not_dok3: A longer confidence-interval, test-statistic, or chi-square calculation with the correct procedure already named; more arithmetic does not add strategic thinking.
A conditions checklist that asks only whether each inequality is at least 10 or whether a sample is below 10 percent of the population.
An interpretation prompt that supplies the correct conclusion and asks the student to restate it in context.
Lettered parts that separately compute, check, and conclude but never ask the student to adjudicate a procedure, interpretation, or scope claim.
